agent_blocked_on.topic: batch_scan.py lowercase_in_target is computed case-insensitively and is unusable as written
agent_blocked_on.detail: batch_scan.py:132 lowercases the whole target ('target_lower') and line 147 then searches it for the lowercased token. The search therefore matches the token in ANY case, so the flag is True for 96 of this directory's 153 members whose wrong-form never appears lowercase at all - including Velphina, Brewbrewry, Vucarydin and Somna. Applied literally, the brief's rule ('if it is true, recommend no_rule') would suppress every genuine correction in this chapter. I recomputed the test case-sensitively (search the raw target for the all-lowercase form as a standalone word) and used that; 40 members are genuinely lowercase and all 40 are ordinary English words, which is exactly what the rule is meant to catch. Every member carries both values: 'lowercase_in_target' (recomputed, authoritative) and 'lowercase_in_target_as_scanned' (the raw flag). ORCHESTRATOR DECISION NEEDED: this defect is in the shared script, so all 14 agents inherit it; confirm the recomputation before merging any directory's rows.

agent_notes.topic: kind convention for out-of-game proper nouns
agent_notes.detail: Where BOTH transcriptions independently render the same non-campaign proper noun (Katie, Raphael, Shadowheart, Gale, Baldur's Gate Act One, Linux, Razor, Viva Las Vegas), I classed the sibling as 'ordinary_words' rather than 'different_name'. Reasoning: the documented contamination SUBSTITUTES a name it already knows; it does not agree with the target. Agreement is therefore corroboration that the word was spoken, and the operative conclusion - no CAMPAIGN name was spoken at this span - is exactly what ordinary_words licenses. 'different_name' is reserved for spans where the sibling shows a campaign-plausible name DIFFERENT from ours (cluster 24 is the only one here).
